title: Signed three-trial grip change did not establish incremental depression-screen prediction across NHANES samples
abstract: We tested whether trial order contains depression-related physiological information discarded by peak grip strength. Models trained in 4,205 adults from NHANES 2011–2012 were frozen and evaluated in 4,692 independently sampled 2013–2014 adults. Adding signed first-to-third change to conventional strength and demographic predictors changed weighted Brier loss by −0.00005956 (conditional stratified-PSU 95% interval −0.00042818 to +0.00031783). Beyond unordered variability and asymmetry, the change was +0.00010372 (−0.00019321 to +0.00039361). Neither comparison established benefit. The trials usually increased rather than declined. This is a negative incremental-prediction test, not evidence that trial order has no information or that it measures peripheral fatigue. Validation in another study program was not completed.
